f156.summary: Ambrogio Bizozola reports to Maximilian Sforza, then in France, that the Emperor's council has several times discussed dividing the state of Milan among the Duke of Savoy, the Marquises of Monferrato and Mantua and the Duke of Ferrara, and whether Duke Francesco would have to be satisfied. The Emperor is at the Certosa outside Bologna, with his entry the next day (Charles V entered Bologna on 5 November 1529); the letter also deals with misere Iulio, Trivulzio and Alessandro Attavante.
f156.en:
By my last letters from Cremona and [t farbar], and from here, you will have heard many things. I speak of the doings of
Messer [?Giulio], how his affairs with the Emperor have gone, and that many times everything was broken off.

Here I have learned from a man worthy of trust that, because of these [roturi], the Emperor's council has several times
held great discussions about the duchy of Milan, saying that Duke Francesco was negotiating [...] with another.
[?Discussing] it, they spoke of making many parts of the state: to the Duke of Savoy, to the Marquis of Monferrato, to
the Marquis of Mantua, to the Duke of Ferrara, and Milan to Duke Alessandro. In this discussion the Archbishop [luo] of
Bari said: it would be better to give it to Duke [?Massimiliano], to whom it comes by [?right]. Another said:

system: Letter substitution with invented signs, words spaced, a few homophones and one sign serving a/u and one f/s (Lasry key).
